ordered_diagnoses: Pulmonary Atresia with Ventricular Septal Defect

s1.syndrome_frame: cyanotic congenital heart disease with thrombocytopenia
salient_findings: pulmonary atresia with ventricular septal defect
thrombocytopenia with prolonged platelet aggregation time
key_facts: male newborn referred at 1 day of age for cyanosis
oxygen saturation was 80% in room air
hematocrit of 47.8% and platelet count of 103 000/mm3
echocardiography revealed pulmonary atresia with ventricular septal defect
patent ductus arteriosus
prostaglandin infusion raised SaO2 to 90-95%
systemic-to-pulmonary shunt operation performed on day 11
postoperative platelet count increased without transfusion
thrombocytopenia persisted at 10 months of age
platelet aggregation time was 127 s
antiplatelet antibodies and platelet-associated immunoglobulins were negative

shortlist.label: Pulmonary Atresia with Ventricular Septal Defect
shortlist.why_kept: Echocardiography revealed pulmonary atresia with ventricular septal defect

shortlist.label: Tetralogy of Fallot
shortlist.why_kept: Cyanosis and pulmonary atresia are consistent with tetralogy of Fallot spectrum

shortlist.label: Thrombocytopenia-Absent Radius Syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Thrombocytopenia and congenital heart disease are features of this syndrome

shortlist.label: Alagille Syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Congenital heart disease and thrombocytopenia can be seen in Alagille Syndrome

shortlist.label: Congenital Amegakaryocytic Thrombocytopenia
shortlist.why_kept: Thrombocytopenia and normal platelet aggregation time are consistent with this diagnosis

raw.rationale: The patient had persistent thrombocytopenia since birth, with a platelet count of 103 000/mm3 at 1 day of age and 68 000/mm3 at 10 months of age, and normal platelet aggregation time was prolonged at 127 s, which suggests a congenital thrombocytopenia, and the absence of other explained causes of thrombocytopenia

rejected.label: Pulmonary Atresia with Ventricular Septal Defect
rejected.why: Although the patient has pulmonary atresia with ventricular septal defect, this does not explain the persistent thrombocytopenia

rejected.label: Tetralogy of Fallot
rejected.why: Tetralogy of Fallot does not typically present with thrombocytopenia

rejected.label: Thrombocytopenia-Absent Radius Syndrome
rejected.why: There is no mention of absent radius in the patient's presentation

rejected.label: Alagille Syndrome
rejected.why: Alagille Syndrome typically presents with liver disease, heart disease, and other systemic abnormalities, which are not mentioned in the patient's presentation
